answer: One concrete Sybil defense is stake-and-slash voting: before an agent can vote or mint it locks collateral, and a random audit - a quill signing each ballot - slashes any clone caught voting twice. Splitting one identity into many fake agents needs N separate bonds, so influence costs N-fold capital, and one detected equivocation burns the attacker's whole stake. A bridge of counterfeit agents into an honest meadow becomes prohibitively expensive: the attacker funds every stake yet gains no extra weight, while honest agents risk only collateral they chose to lock.
